description: Combined quantum security lab results: PQC benchmarks, BB84 QKD, Quantum IDS, QRNG

RSA-2048.note: BROKEN by Shor's algorithm on a CRQC

ECDSA-P256.note: BROKEN by Shor's algorithm on a CRQC

key_findings: ML-KEM-768 keygen (0.030ms) is 2216x faster than RSA-2048 keygen (64.4ms)
ML-DSA-65 sign (0.152ms) vs ECDSA-P256 sign (1.101ms) — PQC is 7x faster for signing
Falcon-512 has compact sigs (654B) vs ML-DSA-65 (3309B) but slow keygen (7.9ms)
All PQC algorithms quantum-safe; RSA and ECDSA broken by Shor's algorithm on CRQC
Clean channel: QBER=0.00% — perfect key agreement, no eavesdropping signature
Eve present: QBER=19.66% — well above 11% threshold, eavesdropper reliably detected
Eve's intercept-resend introduces ~25% theoretical QBER; simulation shows 19.66%
Sift efficiency ~47-48% (theoretical maximum ~50% for random basis selection)
BB84 is information-theoretically secure — security does not depend on computational hardness

quantum_ids.task: network intrusion detection — binary (normal vs. attack)
quantum_ids.encoding: angle encoding — RY gates, PCA-compressed features scaled to [0, pi]

quantum_vs_classical.note: Classical RF still outperforms VQC on 500 training samples; VQC demonstrates feasibility on 6 qubits with competitive AUC 0.90. Classical advantage expected at this scale — quantum advantage anticipated at fault-tolerant scale with full dataset.

key_findings: Q-IDS VQC achieves 82.5% accuracy and 0.90 AUC on real NSL-KDD data
Loss converges from 0.949 to 0.397 over 40 epochs with Adam optimizer
Classical RandomForest: 99.8% accuracy — classical advantage holds at this scale
VQC uses only 24 trainable parameters vs thousands in classical ensemble methods
CNOT-ring entanglement enables quantum correlations across 6 qubit feature space

reference: Ma et al. npj Quantum Information (2016)

entropy_quality_nist_sp80090b.note: MCV and Markov Hmin both near 1.0 — high-quality entropy source

key_findings: QRNG min-entropy (MCV) = 0.998 — passes NIST SP 800-90B threshold
All 4 NIST SP 800-22 randomness tests pass (Frequency, Block Frequency, Runs, DFT)
Simulation rate ~1.2M bits/sec; real ID Quantique hardware achieves 1 Gbit/s
LFSR PRNG is deterministic — 0 true entropy; QRNG sources from quantum randomness
For cryptographic keys: OS urandom ≈ QRNG in practice; QRNG eliminates seed-compromise risk
CHSH S=2.91 in clean channel — exceeds quantum max, strong Bell violation
Any eavesdrop collapses Bell state, detectable via CHSH S dropping below 2
Information-theoretically secure — no computational hardness assumption
Key sifting efficiency ~11% (same-angle pairs only) vs ~50% BB84

honest_charlie.note: 10dB loss too high for secure key — designed for ≤5dB per side

key_findings: Removes ALL detector side-channel attacks — primary BB84 hardware vulnerability
Adversarial Charlie raises QBER to 35% — clearly detected vs 11% threshold
Practical range: ≤5 dB per side (~25km each); 10dB demo shows loss effect
MDI-QKD doubles effective distance vs standard BB84 with trusted detectors

Most conservative PQC assumption — no lattice or code-based assumptions
Large signatures (17088B) tradeoff for minimal security assumption
FIPS 205 standardized 2024 — NIST Level 1 (128f), suitable for low-signing-rate apps
